Category navigation changes no setting and sends no account operation. Removed diagnostics and compatibility sections remain unavailable through navigation while stable legacy hooks stay mounted outside the visible Settings surface.

Changing category and closing/reopening retain the original mounted controls, unsent form values, nested disclosure state and per-category reading position. Keyboard focus remains within Settings while it is open.

An open native modal cannot be hidden by category navigation. Closing Settings closes its owned account modals. Existing native conversation shortcut dialogs remain usable from a hidden category or a closed Settings surface.

Session full-access and destructive confirmations use a centered borderless card no wider than 560px with viewport clearance and internal overflow; the overlay never stretches the card across the application.

English labels and explanations identify shared Codex workspace access, conversation preferences and Supervisor tool confirmations separately. Protocol diagnostics, model/profile inventories, account token activity, workspace messages, reported thread settings, saved defaults and storage internals are absent from user Settings.

The wide reading column and centered navigation remain bounded on large screens. Narrow layouts keep the compact title/back row and both navigation levels above content as scrolling horizontal selectors; forms, descriptions and primary actions have no horizontal overflow in either theme.
Navigation and the active category are immediately distinguishable.

A distinct five-level type hierarchy orders the page heading, page subtitle, section headings, control names and supporting explanations. Each control explanation sits below its name rather than alongside it, with lighter weight and smaller type; scope labels remain secondary and selector values stay legible. The order and spacing persist in both themes and at narrow and wide widths.
Opening and closing settings never exposes an unthemed frame.

Graph -> Settings -> close returns the usable Supervisor logo, never clipped node-count text. The graph is collapsed in both Rust and the DOM before launcher bounds are restored; reopening still works and preserves graph data and conversation drafts.
Every control has four equivalent corners and no accented border segment.
Codex setup distinguishes connecting, signed out, pending device/browser login, signed in and unavailable catalog states; it does not imply turn support.

The Codex account card explains Supervisor's separate history, settings and sign-in. A first connection can require sign-in despite a connected official Codex app; the sign-out dialog explains the Supervisor-only scope and preserves project/history data. Both descriptions remain readable in Light/Dark and supported layouts.

Reopening a previously connected profile shows Connecting, then Checking/Refreshing, then ChatGPT connected after authoritative native reads, without opening sign-in or replaying work. In main and graph provider details, checking never asks for another login. Explicit sign-out prevents startup reconnection, transient connection errors stay actionable, and a definitively missing account shows Sign-in required. Saved connection intent never restores session permission grants.
API-key and Amazon Bedrock account states show the explicit unsupported subscription-only policy without reading or forwarding their credentials.
Managed permission-profile inventory stays internal. Named requirements keep incompatible presets blocked with a useful explanation; no control claims the experimental thread/start permissions field.
ChatGPT rate-limit buckets distinguish loading, current, stale and unavailable values. A sparse native update causes an authoritative read instead of being merged into the UI.
Account usage, workspace messages, provider capability flags and model upgrade inventories are not shown as preferences. Their internal values never imply account or tool permission.

Configuration, deprecation, general runtime and Windows world-writable warnings appear as bounded actionable text; stale notices are labelled and unknown payload fields and protocol diagnostics are absent.

The device code is selectable; only explicit Open sign-in page opens the validated identity URL in the OS default browser. The complete OAuth query is preserved without a file-manager or command-shell launch. Browser launch failures remain actionable in the pending sign-in without exposing the URL in errors. Cancel and sign-out confirmation stay keyboard-accessible.

scenarios.readerJob: Use newly available Codex and Claude Code models without restarting or losing the current conversation.
scenarios.setup: Both providers have valid catalogs; a refresh adds a model, changes the default, then fails temporarily. Repeat with a graph agent running and with explicit sign-out.
assertions: New runtime-reported models appear in main-chat and graph selectors; a still-valid model, effort, speed and context selection remains unchanged.
Background discovery never switches a ready provider to Checking, sends an inference turn, clears a draft, or inserts chat activity.
A running main-chat or graph provider defers checks and late results, without changing its active profile.
A failed refresh retains the last usable catalog and reports the issue in provider details; explicit sign-out disables execution.

Manual checks bypass the 15-minute refresh interval, without launching duplicate discovery processes. The Windows host discovers the tested official desktop-app binary when no packaged or PATH CLI exists, while an explicit override remains authoritative.

scenarios.readerJob: Retain safe optional App Server operations without exposing protocol controls as user preferences.
scenarios.setup: Connected ChatGPT account, current local project, beta/stable/under-development flags, detected home/project imports with ACK/progress/completion reordered, available and uncertain reset attempts, successful/failed/uncertain text feedback and email states, plus running/stopping/rejected/uncertain/completed sandboxed PTY output.
assertions: Feature flags, imports, credits, feedback and sandboxed-command protocol controls do not appear in user Settings. If a contextual product flow invokes a retained mutation, it is explicitly confirmed and freezes process, project or account scope so later state cannot retarget it.

The project scope follows the active local project automatically and is shown without a Windows extended-path prefix. Feature inventory is freshness-labelled and filterable; only beta and stable entries can change, one named flag at a time, while experimentalApi remains disabled.

Migration shows bounded descriptions, opaque selections and count-only results without raw details, failure messages or arbitrary paths. An accepted import remains busy through progress until authoritative completion, blocks a second mutation or reconnect, and becomes explicitly uncertain after disconnect. Completion wins over a later progress event. A project change invalidates the preview, and uncertain imports direct the user to sanitized history before retry.

Reset redemption requires a current positive available count and reuses one Rust-owned idempotency key after uncertain or malformed delivery. Email nudges distinguish requesting, sent, cooldown, failed and uncertain states without retaining stale progress text.

Feedback confirmation previews the exact bounded text and states that logs, files, paths, tags and conversation content are absent; failed and uncertain delivery are terminal, non-contradictory and never appear as success or an upload still in progress.

The sandboxed command accepts argv rather than a shell string, offers read-only or project-write only, and keeps stdin, resize, termination, bounded output and connection failure under one opaque process identity. A certain terminate rejection restores controls only while the process is live; malformed or delivery-unknown termination remains explicit and cannot be cleared or replaced until completion or disconnect.
No filesystem, injection, single-value config or plugin protocol controls are exposed as settings. Runtime state remains bounded and cannot trigger a model turn by being read.

scenarios.readerJob: Find a native Codex conversation and explicitly link it or create an independent fork in a main chat or local graph agent.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic active/archived history pages, native title search, an unbound local chat with another provider's history, automatic new project/graph branch destinations, changed directory during confirmation, uncertain forks after restart and late results after closing.
assertions: Browsing sends only native thread/list; all pages remain reachable with Load more, and filters/search are explicit.

History, skills, defaults and project diff open in the real NavigateToString host without secure-context-only randomUUID; display-form and canonical Windows paths compare as one project without weakening request correlation, origin or permission authority.
Link and Fork explain shared versus independent native history and never imply file copies or checkpoints.
Archived sources offer Link but disable Fork with an explicit restore explanation; neither opening nor confirming can silently unarchive a conversation.
Import is confirmed against the observed result and original local directory, cannot replace a binding, and preserves the draft and other-provider history.

Fork into a new conversation validates the observed source before saving a local destination. Archived sources cannot create empty chats/cards or fork receipts; an archive event closes a pending confirmation and stale submit is rejected in Rust. Explicit restore stays separate. Open branch preserves the source card and focuses a separate card on the same node or a new project chat. The destination uses Supervisor's shared saved Codex workspace access.
A precise fork may select only a completed turn from the currently loaded source; its exact lastTurnId, directory and shared permission preset are frozen and revalidated before dispatch.
Pending or uncertain forks do not create replacement history or replay a prompt. Recovery links only a user-selected native fork of the original source, including after restart.
A result from another owner or older view cannot populate the dialog; errors, empty results, pending operations and disconnect are readable.

The same keyboard-accessible dialog serves main and graph with neutral shared tokens. Selecting Link or Fork replaces the scrolling result list with a focused, visibly bounded confirmation. Prompt text, native titles, full source paths, opaque IDs and raw transcripts never enter the projected history list; only a bounded project label and operational metadata are displayed.

scenarios.readerJob: Select native skills for the next local-project prompt and explicitly manage shared enablement.
scenarios.setup: Main/graph local directories, enabled and disabled skills, metadata errors, changed inventory, cross-owner replies, pending write, different effective native state and disconnect.
assertions: Opening the dialog lists skills without reading instructions into the chat, fetching icons or sending a model prompt.
Use with next prompt adds a removable owner-scoped reference; selection alone does not send input or change configuration.
Start, Queue and Send now freeze the selected native paths with explicit skill mentions; accepted input cannot consume a newer re-selection of the same path.
Enable/disable is confirmed for the original native path and inventory, with shared Codex configuration scope clearly explained.
Native changes and changed directories revoke old choices; stale and disconnected states are readable and require explicit refresh.
Extra roots require a frozen explicit process-scoped confirmation, accept at most 16 canonical absolute non-secret directories, invalidate discovery, and explain restart/reconnect clearing.
Closing a dialog never cancels or retries a pending write; the effective native state is reported honestly even if different from the requested state.
The neutral keyboard-accessible dialog serves both main and graph owners while preserving drafts, attachments and other providers.

scenarios.readerJob: Choose a native review target and follow the reviewer in the same main or graph conversation.
scenarios.setup: Bound idle main/graph conversations, four review targets, changed directory, rejected scope, preparation cancellation, streaming plan changes, completion before acknowledgement and uncertain delivery after reconnect.
assertions: Review requires confirmation of source, directory, read-only scope and account usage; it never consumes composer drafts or file attachments.
The reviewer model is labelled as native configuration, not the composer selection; invalid targets, archived history, remote paths and changed directories cannot start review.
Stop prevents unsent review intent or interrupts the native turn; uncertain delivery is never replayed and can be inspected through native history.

Entered review is work activity; exited-review text is a safely rendered final answer. A completed phase-less echo in that same turn renders only once through the stable exit row even when pagination reorders it. Raw native items, explicit phases and unrelated messages remain intact. Live plan updates preserve disclosure identity and show actual pending/in-progress/completed states.

Inline review instructions appear once when the supervising turn echoes its worker's exact user item and native prompt placeholder. Independent repeated prompts keep their own rows; timing updates preserve user styling. Completion and paginated reload keep one visible result, readable in both themes and main/graph layouts. Graph prose and Markdown emphasis inherit the message foreground rather than legacy terminal colors, with readable contrast in Light as well as Dark.

Native paginated histories disclose the installed runtime's detached-review rejection. Missing history format is not assumed compatible; creating a fork and reviewing it inline remain explicit separate actions, never a silent fallback. A reported legacy history may use separate delivery and binds only the exact returned reviewThreadId under either response/notification ordering.
Shared neutral controls stay keyboard accessible in both themes, and main/graph owners cannot redirect each other's requests or errors.

scenarios.readerJob: Keep native MCP execution bounded without exposing server administration as a general preference.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic paginated global and independent chat/graph inventories, null runtime status, OAuth-required server, failed refresh, scope replacement during pagination, server startup change and completion before login acknowledgement.
assertions: MCP inventories and server configuration do not appear in AI accounts or Agents & permissions. An inventory is loaded only on contextual request; an unknown runtime state is not treated as connected and a failed page never publishes a partial list.
Tools, resources and templates are metadata disclosures; no tool schema, URI credential, executable HTML or remote icon is rendered.
Reload requires a confirmation bound to the observed inventory and explains refresh queuing and possible server reconnection.

Cancelling and immediately reopening configuration or reload confirmation preserves the newly selected intent even if the old dialog close event arrives late; no write or reload occurs before a new explicit confirmation.

Internal configuration changes freeze server input and native view before confirmation. Saved commands, arguments, URLs and credential values never enter a projected inventory. New servers start disabled; enable, remove and reload remain explicit. Conflicts or disconnect preserve drafts and invalidate edit authority without retry.

Edit connection options is scoped to the observed saved user transport, not an overriding effective layer. Only one typed key is replaced, or an observed optional key explicitly cleared; required fields cannot be cleared and empty lists/false are not deletion. Header environment maps replace their old keys. The confirmation names the new value and warns about retained credentials with a changed destination; reopening after a view change is required. No timeout, filter or reload is set implicitly.
OAuth shows the service name and authorization origin, opens only on user intent and handles early completion or disconnect without replay.

A contextual inventory names its native thread; OAuth start and opening its URL retain exact inventory, server and attempt ownership. Metadata changes cannot discard a pending login and global or sibling completions never complete that attempt.
Native MCP metadata and execution cannot change chat ownership, provider selection or permissions merely by being observed.

scenarios.readerJob: Inspect effective project defaults and knowingly edit shared Codex preferences.
scenarios.setup: Main and graph Codex conversations with layered native defaults, an overriding managed layer, a changed file revision and a pending shared write.
assertions: Automatic compaction counting offers total/body_after_prefix with an explanation of full context versus growth after the retained prefix. Saving and clearing use the same frozen confirmations; no model prompt, live reload or context-monitor reinterpretation follows.
Effective values and base user-file values remain distinct, with configuration origins behind disclosure.
Saving requires confirmation of the exact preference, target file and observed native revision; it sends no prompt and does not reload existing conversations.

Clear saved value appears only for an observed user override and requires its own frozen confirmation. It removes one public key, not project/managed layers or the whole configuration. Empty input, changed saved values, stale views and double clicks cannot clear anything implicitly.
Absent targets, stale reads, owner changes, active work and disconnect cannot grant write authority or trigger replay.
Native conflicts and overrides remain actionable, with explicit Refresh and no raw configuration, credentials or instructions in the view.
The same neutral tokenized dialog remains readable and scrollable in main and graph layouts.

scenarios.readerJob: Open an existing native Codex control from the main or graph composer without submitting a model prompt.
scenarios.setup: Main and two graph conversations, a partial slash draft, disconnected and busy native states, ordinary path/multiline input, and a switched provider.
assertions: The monochrome suggestion menu sits above the input, scrolls within its shared height token and does not overlap or replace the transcript.
Arrow keys wrap selection, Tab completes the shortcut, Enter opens the original control, and Escape, Shift+Enter and IME preserve editing behavior.
Commands reach only their original owner. Rename, archive, fork and review keep their existing confirmations and cannot grant authority through shortcut selection.
Resume browses history without importing it, while skills and config open their existing native inventories without a write or inference.
Unavailable commands retain their draft and explanation. Literal paths, multiline prompts, a leading-space escape and other-provider submissions retain ordinary behavior.
Selecting a shortcut preserves attachments and selected skills; Queue and Send now cannot accidentally submit a recognized command as model text.

Compact context is explicitly confirmed for an idle loaded native history. Resume connection loads the same thread without submitting text; accepted/running/Stop states never imply premature completion, and disconnected outcomes require history review without replay.

scenarios.readerJob: Inspect and explicitly manage a native goal in its original main or graph conversation.
scenarios.setup: Main and two graph conversations, a paused/active/limited goal, live accounting, stale state and pending native writes.
assertions: Goal or /goal opens a neutral shared dialog without starting a prompt or silently resuming a conversation.
Creation is paused, budgets are optional with no default limit, and objective/status/accounting are native observations rather than estimates.
Every write is confirmed against the original owner/thread/project/view; usage updates preserve typed text and scope changes invalidate confirmation.
Pause/complete/remove explain their difference from Stop and file restore. Active state uses the loaded native session, not pending composer changes.
Closing, disconnection or late replies never replay edits, overwrite newer events or clear chat drafts. Unknown outcomes offer explicit Refresh.
The dialog remains keyboard accessible and scrollable in main and graph layouts in both appearance modes.

scenarios.readerJob: Inspect and enlarge a native generated image without losing the conversation.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic main and graph native imageGeneration events, valid embedded PNG/JPEG, failed generation, unavailable result and a decoder error.
assertions: Completed embedded images remain outside the work disclosure while the final answer stays distinct, including after native history reload.
Click opens a neutral enlargement with an accessible Close preview action and native Escape behavior; source colors remain unchanged.
A streaming refresh retains image identity, an open preview, manual transcript scroll and sibling conversation state.
Remote URLs, local paths, unsupported formats and oversized results do not trigger reads or downloads; unavailable and decode-error feedback preserves the original native history.
Main and graph share the same tokenized component, with bounded proportional previews in both appearance modes and all supported layout profiles.

scenarios.readerJob: Find and reopen Codex Cloud chats from the connected ChatGPT subscription without confusing them with local history.
scenarios.setup: A connected subscription account with ready, running and failed cloud tasks, pagination, a multi-attempt diff, a stale owner, malformed cloud metadata and a disconnected runtime.
assertions: Opening Codex history loads local and Cloud inventories automatically while keeping them visibly separate; no API key, Agents API request or model turn is created.
Every Cloud row has a cloud icon and shows its bounded title, environment, status, update time, attempts and change totals without presenting an opaque task ID as its label.
Refresh and Load more preserve task identity, deduplicate moving results and reject repeated cursors or late replies from another owner or closed view.
View changes requests only the observed attempt through the official subscription CLI and renders a bounded read-only unified diff; it never applies files or creates a local checkpoint.

Open chat and New cloud chat navigate only to validated ChatGPT Codex HTTPS pages in a real Supervisor browser tab. Full transcript and follow-up work stay on the first-party page because Cloud tasks are not projected as local App Server threads.
Invalid URLs, identities, oversized output, missing sign-in and unsupported runtimes remain explicit errors. Local history, drafts, permissions and project files are unchanged.
The source switch, task states and diff remain keyboard readable in both themes and narrow, Full HD, 2K and 4K layouts.

scenarios.readerJob: Let every agent continue after closing the window, then stop all work explicitly from the notification area.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic idle, main, graph, delegated Codex, approval, detached-window, checkpoint-finalization and Explorer-restart states.
assertions: Closing the main window hides all Supervisor-owned work windows while preserving the same process, WebViews, native App Server connection, conversations and running agents.
Opening or activating the Supervisor tray icon restores the same live windows and state without reload, restart, duplicate submission or lost streaming output.
The native menu exposes Open Supervisor and the explicit Stop all work and quit action; the standalone transparent Supervisor mark remains recognizable at notification-area size.
Stop all work and quit clears future queued submissions, routes Stop to every active main, graph and delegated native owner, denies pending local actions and interrupts owned commands before exit.
Exit waits for native interruption acknowledgement, provider cancellation and Time Machine finalization, with a bounded fallback that terminates only remaining Supervisor-owned work.
An Explorer restart recreates exactly one tray icon; a tray failure restores the main window so Supervisor cannot become inaccessible.
Acceptance instances without a tray retain deterministic close-and-exit behavior, and repeated close, open and quit actions remain idempotent.

scenarios.readerJob: Connect to a VPS desktop, transfer a file, and knowingly grant or stop agent control.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic RDP and VNC profiles, connected desktop canvas, transfer state, and active agent-control indicator.
assertions: The remote canvas receives maximum useful area and scales without distortion.
Connection, transfer, and agent-control states remain visible without obscuring the desktop.
The emergency stop is discoverable and does not rely on color alone.
Application chrome remains monochrome without filtering the remote desktop image.

scenarios.readerJob: Inspect work evidence, compare two attempts and pass native context to a new agent.
scenarios.setup: Two same-project attempts, an idle Codex Supervisor, unrelated project, unloaded/partial history, command failures with and without exit codes, stale reports, fork success and failure. Repeat in Light and Dark at compact, Full HD, 2K and 4K layouts.
assertions: Both conversation action menus expose Work summary, Compare attempts and Hand off without permanent new panels. The project board receives inspection replies even when a chat card is closed; errors or a missing reply end the loading state, and Refresh retries without starting a model turn.

The latest-turn report distinguishes request, reported result, actual command exits, recorded diffs, files and public activity. No outcome is inferred from final prose or turn completion. Unloaded, truncated and missing evidence remain explicit; private reasoning and opaque attachment payloads stay absent.

Comparison shows two distinct same-project attempts. Explicit Ask Supervisor sends one native read-only review to a separate idle initialized Codex Supervisor after report and thread revalidation. Repeated clicks, stale replies and project changes cannot redirect it or apply a patch.

Hand off requires an idle native source, preserves history and attachments through a native fork and saves only an editable continuation draft. Its destination opens inside the board after the native acknowledgement; source drafts, file contents and other conversations are not modified. No model turn starts until the new draft is sent.

The bounded dialog scrolls internally, comparisons stack at narrow widths, focus remains in the modal and Escape closes it. Switching project or closing the board invalidates pending UI state; errors remain actionable. Unknown or failed native fork delivery never becomes a success or an automatic retry.

scenarios.readerJob: Focus and arrange live conversation cards, then create an isolated Git task without losing their state.
scenarios.setup: Synthetic local projects, two open chat cards, one linked Supervisor and worktree IPC. Light/Dark at 1024, 1920, 2560 and 3840 widths.
assertions: Chat and Supervisor bodies mount directly below their own rows; minimizing, focusing and switching projects retain card identity, drafts and stream ownership.
Focus widens one conversation and temporarily compacts the others; Escape restores the previous layout. Columns resize with pointer or keyboard and the file lane can collapse.
Presentation choices stay scoped to each project during the current UI session and never start, stop or alter a turn; they are not written into the native application session.
The selected Supervisor exposes only its supervised-conversation association in one compact menu that overlays the board, remains inside the viewport and closes on Escape or outside interaction.

Git status in a non-Git project reports the reason in the project lane instead of remaining disabled without explanation. In a Git project, Git status and Open terminal reveal a dedicated Supervisor terminal window while the board remains open; output is never sent to the docked terminal hidden behind the board.

New isolated task checks that the source is a Git repository with committed files before opening the native picker, explains that the selected folder is only the parent, and creates a named child worktree from HEAD in a new branch. Non-Git and empty-commit projects show an actionable error without opening the picker or creating a task folder. Existing folders, dirty original files and account data are preserved; no model starts until a prompt is sent.
